sect1.title: Introduction
sect1.para: The ZPrime class, implemented in Cython, is a specialized selection template within the AnalysisG framework, designed for comprehensive analysis of Z' boson related selections in Monte Carlo 16 (MC16) events. It inherits from the generic SelectionTemplate class, extending its functionalities to extract and organize detailed information about truth-level top quarks, children particles, truth-jets, and reconstructed jets associated with Z' boson decays. This class facilitates a high-performance extraction and structuring of Z' boson related data for further physics analysis.

sect1.title: Helper Functions (Python-style, Cython-optimized)
sect1.para: These functions are designed to be used as callbacks for self.root_leaves in SelectionTemplate, processing data as it's read from ROOT files.

listitem.para:
def fx(zp, data): A generic function to append data to a list attribute of the ZPrime instance. It takes an attribute name and a list of values. If the attribute already exists and is a list, it appends the new values; otherwise, it initializes it as a new list.
zp
An instance of ZPrime.
data
A tuple (attribute_name_string, list_of_values) where attribute_name_string is the name of the attribute to update and list_of_values are the values to append.

sect1.title: The ZPrime Class
sect1.para: ZPrime is a cdef class that inherits from SelectionTemplate. It is tailored for collecting and organizing information related to Z' boson analysis.

listitem.para:
__cinit__(self): The Cython "constructor" equivalent.
Initializes self.root_leaves to define specific ROOT branches (zprime_truth_tops, zprime_children, zprime_truthjets, zprime_jets) and associates them with the fx helper function for data processing during InterpretROOT.
Initializes a new C++ zprime object and assigns its pointer to self.ptr. It then upcasts self.ptr to a zprime* and assigns it to self.tt for specialized access.
__init__(self): (Not explicitly defined in the provided snippet) This would typically be the Python initializer.
__dealloc__(self): Deallocates the C++ zprime object pointed to by self.tt, ensuring proper memory management.

cdef void transform_dict_keys(self): This method is responsible for converting the C++ data structures within the underlying zprime object into Python attributes, making them accessible as properties of the ZPrime instance.
self.zprime_truth_tops: Populated from self.tt.zprime_truth_tops.
self.zprime_children: Populated from self.tt.zprime_children.
self.zprime_truthjets: Populated from self.tt.zprime_truthjets.
self.zprime_jets: Populated from self.tt.zprime_jets.

sect1.title: C++ Interaction
sect1.para:
The ZPrime class leverages Cython's capabilities for seamless C++ integration:
cdef class ZPrime: Declares ZPrime as a Cython extension type.
cdef zprime *tt: A C++ pointer to a zprime object, which is the specialized C++ implementation for Z' boson analysis.
self.ptr = new zprime(): Initializes the base SelectionTemplate's C++ pointer.
self.tt = <zprime*>self.ptr: This line demonstrates C++ upcasting, allowing ZPrime to fulfill the SelectionTemplate interface while internally managing its specific zprime data.
from AnalysisG.core.selection_template cimport SelectionTemplate: Imports the base SelectionTemplate class, from which ZPrime inherits.
from AnalysisG.core.tools cimport as_dict, as_list: Imports utility functions for converting between C++ and Python data structures.
